interest: This document is valuable for historians studying pre-World War II Japanese economic expansion and financial networks in Southeast Asia, particularly within the Commonwealth of the Philippines. It demonstrates the regulatory oversight and due diligence conducted by the Philippine Bank Commissioner in cooperation with the U.S. Foreign Service to evaluate major Japanese colonial financial institutions like the Bank of Taiwan. Set against the backdrop of late 1937 during the outbreak of the Second Sino-Japanese War, it also highlights the commercial intelligence role played by U.S. consular posts such as Shanghai under Clarence E. Gauss.
overview: This file contains State Department records under decimal classification 894.51611B concerning branch banks of Japan in the Philippine Islands. The file consists of a single 'List of Papers' docket sheet from 1937 documenting an inquiry by the Bank Commissioner of the Philippines into the financial responsibility, business reputation, and operational methods of the Bank of Taiwan. The docket records a November 29, 1937 report from U.S. Consul General Clarence E. Gauss in Shanghai, who confirmed after investigation that the Bank of Taiwan was a responsible banking institution enjoying a good reputation.

subfiles.about: A State Department list of papers indexing records concerning Japanese branch banks in the Philippines, specifically noting a consular report on the Bank of Taiwan.
subfiles.summary: This docket sheet records Item 1 under subject file 894.51611B regarding Japanese branch banks in the Philippine Islands. It outlines an inquiry by the Bank Commissioner of the Philippines into the standing, responsibility, and commercial conduct of the Bank of Taiwan. It notes that U.S. Consul General Clarence E. Gauss reported from Shanghai on November 29, 1937, concluding after investigation that the bank was a reputable and responsible financial institution.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Branches of Japanese Banks in Philippine Islands
